mainTopic: Why doubtful cases (even with כהנים) are not separated, and the new משנה on the oldest brother's priority in ייבום, including what the word 'בכור' in the פסוק does and does not mean
overview: This amud opens by finishing an answer. Another משנה makes brothers who married separate, but in our case each brother may well have the right woman, so they may stay married. שילא teaches that this holds even if both brothers are כהנים, because a חלוצה is forbidden to a כהן only מדרבנן, and the רבנן made no rule for a ספק חלוצה. The פסוק that seems to teach the ban is only an אסמכתא. A new משנה then teaches that the oldest brother should do ייבום, but if a younger brother goes first, the ייבום counts. A ברייתא reads the ייבום פסוק phrase by phrase: the oldest goes first, an אילונית and a סריס are left out, and 'שם' means inheritance, proven by a גזירה שוה. רבא notes that here the גזירה שוה removes the plain meaning completely. The גמרא then tests several ways to give the בכור a special role and rejects each one: any brother may do ייבום, and his ייבום works. The eldest goes first because of his age, and whoever does ייבום inherits. The amud ends by asking why the תורה says 'בכור' at all, and the answer comes on the next amud.

steps.title: Why the other case requires separation but ours does not
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the difference between another משנה, where brothers who married must separate, and our משנה, where they may stay married. In our case each brother can say he married his own family's woman.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, according to the one who says יש זיקה, the זיקה is real. According to the one who says it is forbidden to cancel the מצוה of ייבום, that is the problem. Here, each brother can say that the woman who came to him is really his own.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is answering a question asked just before this point: why does another משנה force the brothers to separate while our משנה lets them stay married? It gives a reason that works for both opinions about the other case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the other case there is a definite problem, either a real זיקה or the cancelling of the מצות יבמין, so the court separates them. In our case nothing is definite: the confusion means each brother may well have ended up with exactly the right woman. Because of that doubt, the רבנן did not make a rule forcing them apart.

keyTerms.meaning: There, meaning in the other משנה
There is a real bond between the יבמה and the brothers before ייבום
It is forbidden to cancel the מצוה of ייבום
Happens to come to him, falls to him

steps.confusionAlert: The question this answers came just before this section. Do not read הָתָם as our משנה; it points to a different משנה where the brothers must separate.

phrases.aramaic: הָתָם, אִי לְמַאן דְּאָמַר יֵשׁ זִיקָה
phrases.english: There, if it is according to the one who says there is a bond,
phrases.notes: "There" is the other משנה, where brothers who married first must separate.

phrases.english: then there is a bond;

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי לְמַאן דְּאָמַר אָסוּר לְבַטֵּל מִצְוַת יְבָמִין
phrases.english: and if it is according to the one who says it is forbidden to cancel the levirate מצוה,
then it is forbidden to cancel the levirate מצוה.
Here, regarding each and every one,
say that his own one is the one who came to him.
phrases.notes: Each brother may have ended up with the very woman his own brother had married.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָתָם, אִי לְמַאן דְּאָמַר יֵשׁ זִיקָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers a contradiction raised just before this section between two משניות
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases (חילוק): definite problem there, real doubt here
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two משניות seem alike, so both should require separation
steps.terutzMaskana: In the other משנה the problem is definite; in ours each brother may have his proper woman, so there was no גזירה

steps.title: Even if both brothers are כהנים, they need not separate
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's line that if they married first, they are not separated, and brings שילא's teaching that this holds even when both men are כהנים.
steps.simpleTranslation: If they married first, we do not remove them, and so on. שילא taught: and even if both of them are כהנים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to a line of our משנה and adds שילא's ברייתא, which pushes the ruling further: it holds even for כהנים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A כהן may not marry a חלוצה. Since חליצה was done in this case, we might think a כהן who married must divorce her. שילא teaches that even so they are not separated, and this sets up the question of why.

keyTerms.meaning: They went ahead and married first, before asking the court
We do not remove them, so the court does not force them to divorce

phrases.english: If they married first, we do not remove them, etc.
phrases.notes: כּוּ׳ means "and so on". The גמרא quotes only the start of the line from the משנה.

phrases.english: Sheila taught: And even if both of them are priests.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new line of the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Brothers who married first are not separated, even when both are כהנים

steps.title: The reason: a doubtful חלוצה was not forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The reason is that a חלוצה is forbidden to a כהן only מדרבנן, and the רבנן did not make the ban apply to a ספק חלוצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason? A חלוצה is forbidden only מדרבנן, and for a ספק חלוצה the רבנן did not make a גזירה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why כהנים may stay married here, and answers right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two parts to the answer. First, the ban on a חלוצה marrying a כהן is only rabbinic. Second, a rabbinic ban is not stretched to cover a doubtful case, and here it is unclear whether the חליצה was done by her proper יבם.

keyTerms.meaning: From the רבנן, a rabbinic rule

steps.whyThisMatters: This is an example of a common principle: rabbinic bans are often not applied in cases of doubt.

phrases.english: What is the reason?
A chalutza is forbidden by rabbinic law,

phrases.aramaic: וְסָפֵק חֲלוּצָה לָא גְּזַרוּ בְּהוּ רַבָּנַן.
phrases.english: and regarding a doubtful chalutza, the Sages did not make a decree.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reason for שילא's ruling
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why כהנים do not need to divorce a woman who received חליצה
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ban on a חלוצה is rabbinic, and the רבנן did not apply it to a doubtful case

steps.title: A ברייתא seems to learn the חלוצה ban from a פסוק
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the claim that the ban is rabbinic. A ברייתא learns from the word ״וְאִשָּׁה״ in the פסוק that a חלוצה is forbidden to a כהן, just like a גרושה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is a חלוצה really only rabbinic? But a ברייתא teaches: ״גרושה״ — I only know about a גרושה. How do I know about a חלוצה? The פסוק says ״ואשה״.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the reason given in the last step by quoting a ברייתא that seems to make the חלוצה ban a Torah law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the ban came from the Torah, it would apply even in a case of doubt, and שילא's ruling for כהנים would fall apart. The ברייתא reads the extra word ״וְאִשָּׁה״ as adding the חלוצה to the גרושה.

keyTerms.meaning: But was it not taught in a ברייתא? This opens a challenge
A divorced woman, forbidden to a כהן

phrases.english: And is a chalutza really forbidden by rabbinic law?
But it was taught: "Divorced"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 21:7

phrases.english: I have only a divorcée;
from where do I know a chalutza?
The verse states: "And a woman"!
phrases.notes: The extra word "woman" is read as adding the חלוצה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the claim made in step 3
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the ban on a חלוצה marrying a כהן is rabbinic
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא learns the ban from a פסוק, which suggests it is Torah law and would apply even in doubt

steps.title: The verse is only a support for a rabbinic rule
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ban really is rabbinic, and the פסוק is only an אסמכתא, a support hint.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is מדרבנן, and the פסוק is just an אסמכתא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends its reason by explaining that the ברייתא's use of the פסוק does not make the ban Torah law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Sometimes the רבנן attach their rule to a פסוק as a hint, called an אסמכתא, without the פסוק truly creating the law. So the ban stays rabbinic, and the rule that it does not apply to a ספק חלוצה still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Merely a support: a פסוק used as a hint for a rabbinic rule

steps.whatToRemember: A חלוצה is forbidden to a כהן מדרבנן, and the פסוק ״וְאִשָּׁה״ is only an אסמכתא. That is why כהנים who married in this doubtful case are not separated.
steps.confusionAlert: When a ברייתא brings a פסוק, it does not always mean the law is from the Torah. Here the פסוק is only a hint for a rabbinic rule.

phrases.english: It is by rabbinic law,
and the verse is merely a support.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִדְּרַבָּנַן הוּא, וּקְרָא אַסְמַכְתָּא בְּעָלְמָא הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from step 4
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the source as an אסמכתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא's derivation makes the חלוצה ban a Torah law
steps.terutzMaskana: The ban is rabbinic; the פסוק is only a supporting hint

steps.title: New משנה: the oldest brother should do ייבום first
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה teaches that the oldest brother has the first right to do ייבום, but if a younger brother does it first, the ייבום works.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a מצוה for the oldest brother to do ייבום. But if the younger one went first, he has acquired her.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It teaches the order of preference among brothers for ייבום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The oldest brother comes first as a matter of מצוה. This order is only a preference, though: a younger brother who does ייבום first truly acquires the יבמה.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה, the start of a new משנה
The מצוה belongs first to the oldest brother
Acquired, so the ייבום is valid

phrases.english: MISHNA:
It is a מצוה for the eldest to perform levirate marriage,
and if the younger one went first, he has acquired her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה, unrelated to the previous discussion
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The oldest brother has the first right to do ייבום, but if a younger brother does it first, it is valid

steps.title: A ברייתא reads the ייבום verse phrase by phrase
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא learns three things from the פסוק: the oldest brother comes first for ייבום, an אילונית is left out, and the יבם inherits his dead brother's property.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: 'And it shall be that the firstborn': from here we learn that the מצוה of ייבום is on the oldest brother. 'That she bears': this leaves out an אילונית, who cannot have children. 'Shall be established in the name of his brother': this is about inheritance.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that finds a source for the משנה's rule that the oldest brother comes first. Along the way, it learns two more laws from the same פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'הבכור' is read as describing the brother who does ייבום, so the oldest brother has the first right. 'אשר תלד' shows that ייבום applies only to a woman who is able to have children. 'יקום על שם אחיו' is read as inheritance, which sets up the question that comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: The רבנן taught; this opens a ברייתא
Firstborn; here it is read as the oldest brother
A woman who cannot have children

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read 'הבכור' here as the baby who will be born. The ברייתא reads it as the oldest living brother, who has the first right to do ייבום.

phrases.english: GEMARA: The Sages taught:
"And it shall be that the firstborn"
phrases.notes: דברים 25:6

phrases.english: from here we learn that the mitzvah to do ייבום is on the oldest.
"That she bears"
excludes an aylonit, who does not give birth.
"Shall be established in the name of his brother"
for inheritance.
phrases.notes: He means the brother who does ייבום inherits the dead brother's property.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the פסוק source for the משנה's rule (step 6) that the oldest brother comes first.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The oldest brother comes first for ייבום, an אילונית has no ייבום, and the יבם inherits his brother.

steps.title: Maybe 'name' means naming the child
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks whether 'יקום על שם אחיו' might mean giving the child the dead brother's name, such as יוסף or יוחנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do you say it means inheritance? Or maybe it only means the name: if the dead brother was יוסף, they call the child יוסף; if he was יוחנן, they call him יוחנן.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא questions its own reading. It raises the more obvious meaning of 'name' and sets up the proof that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Read simply, 'יקום על שם אחיו' sounds like naming the child after the dead brother. The ברייתא has to explain why it chose 'inheritance' over this simpler reading.

keyTerms.meaning: Do you say...? This opens a challenge to a reading
Or perhaps it is only...; this offers another possible reading

phrases.english: Do you say it is for inheritance,
or is it only for the name:
if he was Yosef, they call him Yosef,
phrases.notes: The 'him' here is the child born from the ייבום.

phrases.english: if he was Yochanan, they call him Yochanan.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַתָּה אוֹמֵר לְנַחֲלָה, אוֹ אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא לְשֵׁם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the 'inheritance' reading from step 7.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does 'שם' in the פסוק mean inheritance or the actual name given to the child?

steps.title: A גזירה שוה proves 'name' means inheritance
steps.stepSummary: The word 'שם' also appears in a פסוק in בראשית, where it clearly means inheritance, so here too it means inheritance.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here it says 'shall be established in the name of his brother,' and there it says 'they shall be called after the name of their brothers in their inheritance.' Just as 'name' there means inheritance, 'name' here means inheritance too.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers its own question with a גזירה שוה, a word that appears in two places.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In בראשית, 'name' is tied directly to inheritance. Because the same word appears in the ייבום פסוק, it carries the same meaning there. That rules out the 'naming the child' reading.

keyTerms.meaning: Learning a meaning from the same word appearing in two פסוקים

phrases.english: It says here, "shall be established in the name of his brother,"
and it says there:
"they shall be called after the name of their brothers in their inheritance,"
phrases.notes: בראשית 48:6

phrases.english: just as 'name' stated there means inheritance,
so too 'name' stated here means inheritance.

steps.triggerLanguage: נֶאֱמַר כָּאן ״יָקוּם עַל שֵׁם אָחִיו״, וְנֶאֱמַר לְהַלָּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 8.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Through a גזירה שוה with בראשית 48:6, 'שם' means inheritance and not naming the child.

steps.title: A סריס has no ייבום
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא learns from 'ולא ימחה שמו' that there is no ייבום when the dead brother was a סריס.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And his name will not be blotted out': this leaves out a סריס, whose name is already blotted out.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא goes back to reading the rest of the פסוק and learns one more law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ייבום exists so that the dead brother's name is not wiped out. A סריס could never have had children, so his name is already wiped out, and ייבום does not apply to his wife.

keyTerms.meaning: A man who cannot have children

phrases.english: "And his name will not be blotted out"
excludes a eunuch, whose name is already blotted out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the phrase-by-phrase reading begun in step 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is no ייבום for the wife of a סריס.

steps.title: רבא: here the plain meaning is fully set aside
steps.stepSummary: רבא notes that usually a פסוק never loses its plain meaning, but here the גזירה שוה removes the plain meaning completely.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Even though in the whole Torah a פסוק never leaves its plain meaning, here the גזירה שוה came and took it away from its plain meaning completely.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא makes a general comment about the ברייתא's reading. This case is a rare exception to a famous rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a דרשה adds a meaning while the simple meaning stays true. Here the גזירה שוה makes 'name' mean only inheritance. So there is no מצוה at all to name the child after the dead brother.

keyTerms.meaning: A פסוק never loses its plain meaning

steps.whatToRemember: The rule 'אין מקרא יוצא מידי פשוטו' has an exception here. In ייבום, the גזירה שוה makes 'שם' mean inheritance only, and the child is not required to get the dead brother's name.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a famous source for the rule that a פסוק keeps its plain meaning, and it shows that the rule can have exceptions.

phrases.english: Rava said:

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דִּבְכׇל הַתּוֹרָה כּוּלָּהּ
phrases.english: Even though in the entire Torah
a verse does not leave its plain meaning,
here the gezeira shava came
phrases.notes: This is the גזירה שוה from step 9, which ties 'name' to inheritance.

phrases.english: and took it out of its plain meaning completely.
phrases.notes: The simple reading, naming the child after the dead brother, is dropped entirely.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: אַף עַל גַּב דִּבְכׇל הַתּוֹרָה כּוּלָּהּ אֵין מִקְרָא יוֹצֵא מִידֵי פְשׁוּטוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Comments on the גזירה שוה from step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the ייבום פסוק, the גזירה שוה fully replaces the plain meaning of 'שם'.

steps.title: Could 'name' ever have meant an actual name?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבא: the plain reading of 'שם' as a real name does not fit the wording of the פסוק at all, so why say the גזירה שוה was needed to remove it?
steps.simpleTranslation: Without the גזירה שוה, would I really have said that 'name' means an actual name? Who is the תורה talking to? If it is talking to the יבם, it should have said 'your brother'. If it is talking to the בית דין, it should have said 'his father's brother'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions רבא's statement from the last step. It argues the plain meaning, 'give the baby the dead brother's name', never worked with the wording of the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says 'יקום על שם אחיו', 'on the name of HIS brother'. If the תורה were speaking to the יבם, it would say 'your brother'. If it were speaking to the בית דין about the baby, the dead man is the baby's uncle, so it would say 'his father's brother'. Since neither fits, the plain reading seems impossible, and then the גזירה שוה did not really remove anything.

keyTerms.meaning: Learning one פסוק from another because they use the same word
The תורה is commanding or instructing

phrases.english: And if not for the גזירה שוה,
would I have said that 'name' means an actual name?
Whom is the Merciful One instructing?
If the יבם, 'shall rise on the name of your brother'
phrases.notes: The פסוק actually says 'his brother'. The גמרא says that if it were talking to the יבם, it would say 'your brother'.

phrases.english: is what it should have said!
If it is speaking to the court,

phrases.aramaic: ״יָקוּם עַל שֵׁם אֲחִי אָבִיו״ מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ!
phrases.english: it should have said 'shall rise on the name of his father's brother'!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי לָאו גְּזֵרָה שָׁוָה, הֲוָה אָמֵינָא ״שֵׁם״ — שֵׁם מַמָּשׁ?
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבא's claim in step 11 that the גזירה שוה removed the plain meaning
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's statement that the גזירה שוה took the פסוק away from its plain meaning
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The plain meaning does not fit the grammar of the פסוק whether it addresses the יבם or the בית דין, so there was no plain meaning for the גזירה שוה to remove.

steps.title: The plain meaning was possible, so the גזירה שוה removed it completely
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the תורה may be telling the בית דין to tell the יבם 'name the baby after his brother'. So the plain reading could work, and it took the גזירה שוה to remove it completely.
steps.simpleTranslation: Maybe this is what the תורה is telling the בית דין: 'Tell the יבם: let the baby rise on the name of his brother.' But the גזירה שוה came and took the פסוק away from its plain meaning completely.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבא by showing the wording 'his brother' does fit. The תורה speaks to the בית דין, who pass a message on to the יבם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the בית דין is speaking to the יבם about the dead man, 'his brother' is exactly the right word. So the plain reading, giving the baby the dead brother's name, was a real option. That shows the גזירה שוה really did remove that plain meaning, just as רבא said.
steps.whatToRemember: Here the plain meaning of 'יקום על שם אחיו' (naming the baby) was a real option, but the גזירה שוה with בראשית removes it completely. 'שם' here means inheritance only.

phrases.aramaic: וְדִלְמָא הָכִי קָאָמַר לְהוּ רַחֲמָנָא לְבֵית דִּין:
phrases.english: And perhaps this is what the Merciful One is saying to the court:
Say to the יבם:
'Let him rise on the name of his brother.'
Rather, the גזירה שוה came
and took it out of its plain meaning completely.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְדִלְמָא הָכִי קָאָמַר לְהוּ רַחֲמָנָא לְבֵית דִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 12 and confirms רבא's statement
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-reading who the פסוק is addressing
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The wording 'his brother' fits neither the יבם nor the בית דין, so the plain meaning was never possible.
steps.terutzMaskana: The תורה tells the בית דין to tell the יבם, so 'his brother' fits. The plain meaning was possible, and the גזירה שוה removed it completely.

steps.title: Maybe only the firstborn brother may do ייבום
steps.stepSummary: Since the ברייתא read the פסוק as talking about the oldest brother, the גמרא suggests that only the בכור may do ייבום and a regular brother may not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now that you say the פסוק is written about the oldest brother, say that the בכור does ייבום, and a regular brother does not do ייבום!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the ברייתא from step 7, which said the oldest brother comes first. It asks whether that means only the oldest brother is allowed to do ייבום at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא learned from 'הבכור' that the oldest brother goes first. The גמרא pushes this further: maybe the פסוק makes the בכור the only one who can do ייבום. Then if there is no בכור, no one could do it.

keyTerms.meaning: A regular brother, not the firstborn

phrases.english: Now that you have said
that the verse is written about the oldest brother,
phrases.notes: This is 'והיה הבכור אשר תלד', the פסוק the ברייתא used back in step 7.

phrases.english: say: the firstborn does ייבום,
and a regular brother does not do ייבום!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the first teaching of the ברייתא in step 7 and challenges it
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's reading that the פסוק speaks about the oldest brother
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the פסוק is about the בכור, maybe it limits ייבום to the בכור alone, not just giving him priority.

steps.title: The exclusion of a later-born brother proves other brothers can do ייבום
steps.stepSummary: If only the בכור could do ייבום, the תורה would not need to exclude a brother who was born after the dead brother died. That brother could never be the בכור anyway.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, why would I need the rule that the תורה excluded the wife of a brother who did not live in the same world as him?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by pointing to a different rule. The תורה excludes a brother who was not alive together with the dead brother, and that rule would be pointless if only the בכור could do ייבום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A brother born after the dead brother had already died can never be the oldest. If ייבום were only for the בכור, he would be left out automatically, and the תורה would not need a special exclusion for him. Since the תורה does exclude him, other younger brothers must be able to do ייבום. The בכור just goes first.

keyTerms.meaning: The wife of a brother who was not alive at the same time as him

steps.whatToRemember: Any brother can do ייבום. The oldest only gets priority, as shown by the separate exclusion of a brother who never lived at the same time as the dead brother.
steps.confusionAlert: The proof works because a later-born brother can never be the בכור. That is why excluding him would be pointless if only the בכור did ייבום.

phrases.english: If so,
the wife of his brother who was not in his world,
phrases.notes: A brother born only after the dead brother had already died, so the two were never alive at the same time.

phrases.english: whom the Merciful One excluded,
phrases.notes: From 'כי ישבו אחים יחדו', דברים 25:5.

phrases.english: why do I need it?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם כֵּן, אֵשֶׁת אָחִיו שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה בְּעוֹלָמוֹ דְּמִיעֵט רַחֲמָנָא — לְמָה לִי?
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 14
steps.terutzResolutionType: Proof from a different exclusion that would otherwise be unnecessary
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only the בכור may do ייבום, and a regular brother may not.
steps.terutzMaskana: Since the תורה needed to exclude a brother who never lived at the same time as the dead brother, ordinary brothers must be able to do ייבום. The בכור only has priority.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that ייבום is a מצוה for all the brothers, with the oldest going first, rather than a מצוה belonging only to the firstborn.

steps.title: רב אחא: maybe the exclusion is about the mother's firstborn
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא challenges the answer of Step 15. Maybe the exclusion of a brother born after the death is needed for a brother who is his mother's בכור.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא challenges: But say the verse comes to exclude the firstborn of the mother!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא attacks the answer from Step 15. He says a brother born after the death could still be a בכור, namely his mother's בכור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 15 said a brother born after the death could never be the בכור, so the exclusion proves any brother can do ייבום. רב אחא answers that if the father had two wives, a later-born son could be his mother's first child. So even under the idea that 'only the בכור does ייבום', the תורה might need to exclude him.

keyTerms.meaning: the mother's firstborn (first child of his mother)

phrases.english: Rav Acha challenges:
But say it comes to exclude the firstborn of the mother!
phrases.notes: He means a son who is his mother's first child but not his father's first, like when the father had two wives.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer given in Step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in Step 15 that the exclusion would be pointless if only the בכור could do ייבום.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A brother born after the death could still be a בכור of his mother, so the exclusion would still be needed.

steps.title: ייבום follows inheritance, which comes from the father
steps.stepSummary: The mother's בכור does not matter. ייבום is tied to inheritance, and inheritance goes through the father only.
steps.simpleTranslation: You cannot say that, since the Merciful One made ייבום depend on inheritance, and inheritance comes from the father and not from the mother.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects רב אחא's idea. The 'בכור' that matters for ייבום is the father's בכור, because ייבום is linked to inheritance.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה tied ייבום to inheritance (״יָקוּם עַל שֵׁם אָחִיו״ was read as נחלה). Inheritance comes only from the father, so being the mother's first child means nothing here. So a later-born brother could never count as the relevant בכור, and the proof from Step 15 stands.

keyTerms.meaning: the Torah made it depend on

phrases.english: That you cannot say
since the Merciful One made ייבום depend on inheritance,

phrases.aramaic: וְנַחֲלָה מִן הָאָב וְלֹא מִן הָאֵם.
phrases.english: and inheritance comes from the father and not from the mother.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב אחא's challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows that the challenger's case does not fit the category.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The mother's בכור might count as a בכור for ייבום.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only the father's בכור counts, because ייבום follows inheritance, which comes from the father.

steps.title: Maybe ייבום only happens when a firstborn exists
steps.stepSummary: New suggestion: if there is a בכור, any brother may do ייבום. If there is no בכור, there is no ייבום at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say: when there is a firstborn, the מצוה of ייבום can be fulfilled; when there is no firstborn, the מצוה of ייבום cannot be fulfilled!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries another way to give the בכור a role. Maybe ייבום only applies in a family that has a living בכור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 15 showed that the יבם does not have to be the בכור. So the גמרא shifts the idea: perhaps the בכור's presence is a condition for the מצוה itself. Without a בכור, maybe no brother may do ייבום.

keyTerms.meaning: the מצוה of ייבום can be fulfilled

phrases.english: But say: when there is a firstborn
the mitzva of ייבום can be fulfilled,
when there is no firstborn
the mitzva of ייבום cannot be fulfilled!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a new way to give the בכור a special role after Step 15's answer.
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption that any brother does ייבום in every case.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Since the פסוק talks about the בכור, perhaps a living בכור is required for ייבום to apply at all.

steps.title: 'One of them dies' includes the firstborn
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says 'one of them dies' without saying which one. That includes the case where the בכור himself died, and still a younger brother does ייבום.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: 'And one of them dies.' Are we not dealing even with where the firstborn died, and the Merciful One says a younger brother should do ייבום?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers from the words 'one of them'. Any brother who dies, even the בכור, leaves a wife for ייבום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the בכור dies, there is no בכור left in the family. Yet the פסוק still calls for ייבום by a younger brother. So ייבום does not depend on having a בכור alive.

phrases.english: The verse says: "And one of them dies,"
phrases.notes: דברים 25:5

phrases.english: are we not dealing even with where the firstborn died,
and the Merciful One says a younger brother should do ייבום?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 18 from the wording of the פסוק.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Proof from an unspecified phrase in the פסוק.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: ייבום applies only when a בכור is alive.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even when the בכור dies, a younger brother does ייבום.

steps.title: Maybe the verse means only a younger brother died
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: perhaps 'one of them' means a younger brother died, and the בכור is the one who does ייבום.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say it is where a younger brother died, and the Merciful One says the firstborn does ייבום?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges Step 19. Maybe the פסוק is not talking about the בכור dying at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 19 assumed that 'one of them' could be the בכור. The challenge reads it narrowly: a younger brother died, and the living בכור must do ייבום. Then no proof remains that a younger brother can do ייבום.

phrases.english: But say it is where a younger brother died,
and the Merciful One says the firstborn does ייבום?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reading of 'one of them' used in Step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: The proof from 'one of them dies' in Step 19.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The phrase could refer only to a younger brother dying, with the בכור as יבם.

steps.title: The exclusion of a later-born brother proves younger brothers do ייבום
steps.stepSummary: The תורה excluded a brother born after the death. That exclusion only makes sense if younger, non-בכור brothers normally do ייבום.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the Merciful One excluded the wife of his brother who was not in his world.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by going back to the exclusion it already used in Step 15.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A brother born after the death can never be the בכור. If the תורה needed to exclude him, then younger brothers must normally be able to do ייבום. So the narrow reading of Step 20 cannot be right.

keyTerms.meaning: who was not alive at the same time as him

phrases.english: But the Merciful One excluded
the wife of his brother who was not in his world.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 20 by using the exclusion from Step 15 again.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Proof from a separate exclusion in the תורה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only the בכור does ייבום, after a younger brother dies.
steps.terutzMaskana: Younger brothers can do ייבום. Otherwise there would be no need to exclude a brother who could never be the בכור.

steps.title: Maybe a younger brother who goes first does not acquire her if a firstborn exists
steps.stepSummary: Last suggestion: if there is no בכור, a younger brother who acts first acquires the יבמה. If there is a בכור, a younger brother who acts first does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say: when there is no firstborn, if a younger one went first, he acquires her. But if there is a firstborn, if a younger one went first, he does not acquire her!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts that younger brothers can do ייבום. Now it asks whether the בכור at least has priority, so that a younger brother's act fails while a בכור is alive.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question has moved from 'who may do ייבום' to 'does the ייבום take effect'. Maybe the בכור's presence blocks a younger brother. If so, a younger brother who goes ahead would not make the יבמה his wife.

phrases.english: But say: when there is no firstborn,
if a younger one went first, he acquires her.
But if there is a firstborn,
if a younger one went first, he does not acquire her!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵימָא: כִּי לֵיכָּא בְּכוֹר, קְדַם קָטָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts that younger brothers can do ייבום, then suggests the בכור has priority.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that any brother's ייבום takes effect.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Since the פסוק singles out the בכור, maybe his presence makes a younger brother's ייבום fail.

steps.title: All brothers are equal: 'If brothers dwell together'
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק 'If brothers dwell together' compares all the brothers to one another. So a younger brother's ייבום works even when a בכור exists.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: 'If brothers dwell together.' The dwelling of brothers is compared one to the other.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the last suggestion with a פסוק that puts all the brothers on the same level.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'together' teaches that the brothers are equal regarding ייבום. So no brother's ייבום is weaker than another's, and a younger brother who goes first does acquire the יבמה. The בכור has no power to block him.
steps.whatToRemember: The בכור cannot block a younger brother's ייבום. Any brother, even a younger one, may do it, and his ייבום takes effect, because 'brothers dwell together' makes them all equal. The eldest still goes first as a matter of מצוה, as the next steps show.

phrases.english: The verse says: "If brothers dwell together"
phrases.notes: דברים 25:5

phrases.english: the dwelling of brothers is compared one to the other.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 22 and closes the series of attempts to give the בכור a special role.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Proof from a פסוק that makes the brothers equal.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A living בכור blocks a younger brother's ייבום.
steps.terutzMaskana: All brothers are equal, so a younger brother's ייבום takes effect even when there is a בכור.

steps.title: Maybe the eldest only gets a second chance when there is a real firstborn
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the eldest brother is called back to do ייבום only when there is a real בכור. A teaching of אביי קשישא says the eldest is called back in every case, and that is hard to fit with the suggestion.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say this: when there is a firstborn, the court should go back to the eldest. When there is no firstborn, the court does not go back to the eldest. So why did אביי קשישא teach: 'The מצוה of ייבום is on the eldest. If he does not want to, the court goes to his younger brother. If he also does not want to, the court goes back to the eldest'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a new way to limit the eldest brother's priority: maybe it applies only when the eldest is a real בכור. It then points out that אביי קשישא's teaching does not seem to fit that limit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The step before showed that a younger brother's ייבום works even when there is a בכור. Now the question is about priority. If the eldest's priority comes from the word 'בכור', maybe an eldest who is not a real בכור should lose his priority. Yet אביי קשישא says the court goes back to the eldest with no mention of him being a בכור.

keyTerms.meaning: 'But say...': the גמרא offers a different possible reading
The court goes back to the eldest brother
אביי the Elder, an earlier teacher, not the famous אביי
The מצוה of ייבום rests first on the eldest brother

phrases.english: But say: when there is a firstborn,
let the court go back to the eldest.
When there is no firstborn,
the court does not go back to the eldest!
Then why did Abaye the Elder teach:
The mitzva of ייבום is on the eldest;

phrases.aramaic: לֹא רָצָה — הוֹלְכִים אֵצֶל אָחִיו הַקָּטָן,
phrases.english: if he did not want to, the court goes to his younger brother;
if he did not want to, the court goes back to the eldest!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After establishing that a younger brother's ייבום works, the גמרא tests whether the eldest's priority depends on him being a real בכור.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that the eldest brother always has priority and is approached again, even when he is not a בכור.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the source for the eldest's priority is the word 'בכור', the priority should apply only to a real בכור. אביי קשישא's teaching applies it to any eldest brother.

steps.title: The eldest is treated like a firstborn because of his age
steps.stepSummary: The eldest brother is compared to a בכור. A בכור gets his priority because he was born first, and the eldest gets his priority because he is the oldest.
steps.simpleTranslation: The eldest is like a firstborn. A firstborn gets his priority because he is the firstborn. In the same way, the eldest gets his priority because he is the eldest.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the eldest brother's priority does not depend on being a real בכור. His being the oldest is enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'בכור' in the פסוק is read as a model, not a strict requirement. What the תורה cares about is being first in age, so any eldest brother keeps his priority. This explains אביי קשישא's teaching.

keyTerms.meaning: Caused it for him, meaning it gave him his priority

phrases.english: Like a firstborn:
just as a firstborn's status as firstborn gives him his priority,
so too the eldest's status as eldest gives him his priority.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 24.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Comparison: the eldest is compared to the בכור, so the reason for priority is age, not firstborn status.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only a real בכור should have priority, since the פסוק says 'בכור'.
steps.terutzMaskana: Any eldest brother has priority, because being oldest is what counts, just as with a בכור.

steps.title: Maybe only a firstborn who does ייבום inherits his dead brother
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests another limit: a בכור who does ייבום receives the dead brother's נחלה, but an ordinary brother who does ייבום does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say this: when a firstborn does ייבום, he takes the inheritance. When an ordinary brother does ייבום, he does not take the inheritance.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a different way to keep the word 'בכור' meaningful: maybe it matters for who inherits the dead brother.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא has already agreed that any brother can do ייבום and that the eldest has priority. The new question is about money. Maybe the right to inherit the dead brother's property belongs only to a real בכור.

keyTerms.meaning: Inheritance, here the dead brother's property
An ordinary brother, one who is not a בכור

phrases.english: But say: when a firstborn does ייבום,
let him take the inheritance;
when an ordinary brother does ייבום,
let him not take the inheritance.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 25 removed the 'בכור' requirement from priority, the גמרא tries applying the word 'בכור' to inheritance instead.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that any brother who does ייבום inherits the dead brother.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Since the פסוק says 'בכור', perhaps the money right of inheritance belongs only to a real בכור.

steps.title: Whoever does ייבום stands in his brother's place, so he inherits
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says 'he shall stand in the name of his brother.' Any brother who does ייבום has done exactly that, so he inherits.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'He shall stand in the name of his brother.' And this brother has stood in his place.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a פסוק: the brother who does ייבום takes the dead brother's place, and that is what earns the inheritance, whether or not he is a בכור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The inheritance comes from taking the dead brother's place, not from being a בכור. Since an ordinary brother who does ייבום also takes that place, he inherits too.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The פסוק says': introduces a source from the תורה
He shall stand in the name of his brother
And here he has stood (in his brother's place)

steps.whatToRemember: The word 'בכור' in the ייבום פסוק is not a strict requirement. Any brother can do ייבום, the eldest has priority because of his age, and whoever does ייבום inherits because he 'stands in his brother's name.'

phrases.english: The verse says:
"He shall stand in the name of his brother,"
phrases.notes: דברים 25:6

phrases.english: and here he has stood.
phrases.notes: He means: this ordinary brother has taken his dead brother's place too, so he qualifies.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר קְרָא: יָקוּם עַל שֵׁם אָחִיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 26.
steps.terutzResolutionType: פסוק-based: the reason for inheriting is taking the brother's place, and every brother who does ייבום does that.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only a real בכור who does ייבום should inherit.
steps.terutzMaskana: Any brother who does ייבום inherits, because he has 'stood in the name of his brother.'

steps.title: Why does the תורה say 'firstborn' at all?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא sets up a question. If being a real בכור changes nothing, why does the תורה use the word 'בכור'?
steps.simpleTranslation: But then why did the Merciful One call him 'firstborn'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move. After removing every practical difference, it asks what the word 'בכור' in the פסוק is there for. The answer comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 14 to 27 showed that a real בכור is not needed for doing ייבום, for priority, or for inheritance. That leaves the word 'בכור' in the פסוק without an obvious job. The גמרא now asks for its purpose, and the answer comes on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: 'But then...': opens a question that follows from what was just said
The Merciful One, meaning the תורה or ה׳

phrases.english: But then, "firstborn"
that the Merciful One called him, why?
phrases.notes: The word 'why' is not written here, but the גמרא means it. The answer comes on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from steps 25 and 27: since 'בכור' has been shown to change nothing in practice, the גמרא asks why the word appears.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What purpose the word 'בכור' serves in the ייבום פסוק, if a real firstborn is not required.
